messages:
anna: Heads-up: noticed allocator churn under mixed workloads after we enabled direct offload. Allocation flamegraph shows compaction stalls when many tiny handoffs happen.

lee: Can you share the flamegraph / small repro? Is this correlated with GC/free latency or with host paging?

anna: Repro is a 10k-req/sec microbench on small pages (4K); compactor threads spike and eviction latency increases ~3x. Logs show many quick free+handoff sequences.

pradeep: Hypothesis: our handoff path currently moves ownership immediately and then does a synchronous free on source. If theres concurrent eviction, we get racing reclamation.

anna: Right. We discussed atomic state markers before, but I wanted to throw out epoch-based reclamation / RCU-style grace periods as an alternative that avoids per-page CAS on hot paths.

lee: Interesting. Epochs would amortize synchronization: mark page as TRANSFERRED, retire entry, reclaim after all readers pass epoch. But how does this interact with compactor which expects timely frees to reclaim VRAM?

pradeep: Two tradeoffs: (1) latency of reclamation (grace period) vs (2) contention/latency on handoff fast path. For small pages we might accept short bounded epoch (few ms) before reclamation to avoid stalls.

anna: We could do hybrid: fast path sets page->state = TRANSFERRED (relaxed store) and appends page id to a per-thread retire-list. Background epoch thread advances when all worker epoch counters advance. Compactor would consult transient residency: it cannot reuse physical slot until epoch passes.

lee: That solves double-free races without adding CAS on every free, but requires global epoch counters and periodic polling. Also need fast path for emergency reclaim when memory pressure is critical.

pradeep: For emergency reclaim, we can provide a special reclaim path that tries to CAS state->FREE_PENDING and, if it fails because TRANSFERRED is in-flight, fall back to synchronous reclaim (with short stall) or preemptively bump epoch and wait.

anna: Example pseudo for retire:
```
void retire_page(Page *p) {
  p->state = TRANSFERRED; // no CAS on retire path
  thread_retire_list.push(p);
}

// background: on epoch advance
for (p in thread_retire_list) if (p->retire_epoch <= global_epoch) reclaim(p);
```
This keeps hot paths cheap.

lee: We also need to watch for long-lived readers (eg. long inference batches holding k-v cache refs). Those will delay epoch advance. Maybe we track per-tenant reader watermarks and bound the grace window.

pradeep: Agree. Add a max_grace_ms after which we force reclamation by converting TRANSFERRED -> FREE_PENDING with coordination (brief stall). That prevents memory blowout from a rogue long reader.

dev-bot: Perf tip: consider 64-bit epoch counters padded to avoid false sharing.

anna: Telemetry ideas: epoch_advances/sec, avg_grace_ms, retire_list_len, emergency_reclaim_count. We'll need dashboard alerts if retire_list_len grows or avg_grace_ms > threshold.

lee: Also audit interaction with paging: if page backing is moved to host and then retired, we must ensure host page isn't freed until epoch passes. That means host mmap/unmap operations should be deferred similarly.

pradeep: Good catch. For host-backed pages we should maintain a small descriptor object (opaque) whose lifecycle follows epoch reclaim instead of immediate munmap. On reclaim we munmap in background.

anna: Action items: 1) I'll prototype per-thread retire lists + epoch manager behind a runtime flag (anna/epoch-reclaim-flag). 2) Pradeep will sketch emergency_reclaim path and the short-stall fallback. 3) Lee to add paging integration notes and add a unit test that fakes long-lived readers. 4) Dev-bot add perf checklist for padding and counters.

lee: ETA?

anna: Prototype PR by EOD Friday. Tests + canary next week. We'll gate behind flag and run on canary-pool for 48h.

pradeep: Longer-term RFC candidate: unify handoff idempotency + epoch reclamation, and explore hazard-pointer style per-allocator fast-paths for extreme low-latency cases.

ops-bot: Canary pool = pool-bravo has new allocator build. Notifying @eng-oncall.

anna: One more ops note: add a metric for host_unmap_latency tied to retire commits so we can see if unmaps are the bottleneck.

lee: Sounds good. Keep perf-ci runs small to iterate faster.

pradeep: Cool. If prototype shows lower tail latency under small-page workloads, we'll expand. Otherwise fallback to atomic-state + bounded-retry approach.

anna: Thanks everyone. I'll drop the PR link when ready. :rocket:
